short: Canada has no federal horizontal AI law. AIDA died with Bill C-27; in 2026 the government introduced Bill C-36, a privacy bill with automated-decision transparency, and Bill C-34, which sets duties for AI chatbots.
title: Canada AI Laws
subtitle: No federal AI act: PIPEDA binds, and two 2026 bills are before Parliament
body_html:
Status at a glance

No federal AI act; privacy and sector law bind. In the government's own words, "Canada does not have federal horizontal AI legislation." The Artificial Intelligence and Data Act, part of Bill C-27, died on the order paper before the federal election. In the 45th Parliament the government introduced two bills that touch AI: Bill C-36, the Protecting Privacy and Consumer Data Act, on 15 June 2026, which would require organisations to be transparent about automated decision-making for significant decisions; and Bill C-34, the Safe Social Media Act, on 10 June 2026, which would set a duty to act responsibly for AI chatbots. Neither is law. Verified on 25 October 2026 against Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada, Canadian Heritage, Justice Laws and OSFI.

Key instruments

InstrumentNumberIntroduced or publishedIn force
Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents ActS.C. 2000, c. 5In force (current to 30 September 2026)
Protecting Privacy and Consumer Data ActBill C-36, 45th Parliament15 June 2026Not passed
Safe Social Media ActBill C-34, 45th Parliament10 June 2026Not passed
OSFI Guideline E-23, Model Risk ManagementE-2311 September 20251 May 2027

Who regulates and enforces

  • Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada: oversees PIPEDA.
  • Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada, under the Minister of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Innovation: AI policy, and sponsor of Bill C-36.
  • Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI): model risk, including AI and machine learning, in federally regulated financial institutions.
  • The bills would create new enforcers: a Privacy and Consumer Data Commissioner (C-36) and a Digital Safety Commission of Canada (C-34).

Scope and reach

PIPEDA covers private-sector organisations. Bill C-36's backgrounder says organisations would have to assess and mitigate privacy risks before sending personal information outside Canada. Bill C-34 would cover "certain AI chatbot services", a term its release does not define.

Core obligations

  • Today: PIPEDA's privacy duties; OSFI E-23 model risk management, including explainability, bias and drift, from 1 May 2027.
  • Proposed in C-36: be transparent about the use of automated decision-making for significant decisions about individuals.
  • Proposed in C-34: reduce the risk of harmful content and behaviour from AI chatbots, including posing as a human being, interrupt crisis conversations and refer users to human support.

Penalties

BreachMaximumProvisionEnforcer

Proposed: administrative monetary penalties under Bill C-36Up to CAD 10 million or 3% of global revenue, whichever is greaterBill C-36 backgrounder, 15 June 2026Proposed commissioner
Proposed: the most serious offences under Bill C-36Up to CAD 25 million or 5% of global revenue, whichever is greaterBill C-36 backgrounderCourts

What is coming next

  • Further stages of Bills C-36 and C-34 in Parliament. Their current stage could not be read: LEGISinfo answered this crawler 403.
  • The outcome of ISED's consultation on AI transparency, which ran from 23 July to 23 September 2026.
  • 1 May 2027: OSFI Guideline E-23 takes effect.
